write: Boiling, said once, in one place: it is optional; it draws tannin from the outer layer faster; two keepers say it can make wood softer and quicker to rot, and no source says otherwise; for spider wood alone, a shop says it speeds sinking but can soften thin branches and break their tips. Sources differ only on whether boiling helps wood sink: never "boiling does not make wood sink" as a plain fact, never softened branches for all wood, never "sources differ" on rot. Take out "Luộc không làm gỗ chìm, lại làm nhánh mảnh mềm đi, đầu nhánh dễ gãy." and "Các nguồn khác nhau ở chỗ luộc có làm lũa mau mục hay không."
Rot, said once, in one place: which wood lasts and the signs that a piece is rotting. Never "does not rot" beside "may be rotting".
Malaysian driftwood is mangrove root: write "rễ cây ngập mặn", never "đước".
Leave out: hydrogen peroxide and potassium permanganate, the Walstad remark, the 2,000 ppm of tannin, mopani's density and its percentages.
Cholla's item opens with what it is; the shops' sizes go last or out.
Lũa linh sam's own item says it sinks at once and what shops say of the colour it gives the water.
Lũa trà gừng and lũa xương trùm each keep an item of their own, apart from trà rừng and xương chùm, unless a source says they are the same wood.

Put back, where the facts give them, and grow nothing else: the white film peaks in weeks 1–2; only stainless screws, since other metals rust; wood too big for the tank takes the fish's swimming room; never put wood in while it still colours the water.
Manzanita: after the sources differ, say what to do, as the facts give it: soak it weighted for 3–4 weeks.
Malaysian driftwood has no Vietnamese name in the facts: never "lũa Malaysia".

Lũa vân thép and lũa thép: never "cũng mòn tới lõi như săn đá". One shop says "vân thép – san đá" is worn to the core; another calls lũa thép (vân thép) a newer, rough, very hard wood like linh sam. Give each only what its own source says.
Take the bucket line out of the kinds' opening paragraph: "Cách chắc nhất là ngâm thử trong xô, thấy nước hết ra màu rồi hãy cho vào bể." Soaking in a large bucket for 1–2 weeks stays where it is.

Planting before the cycle is stable is not a mistake: one shop says it can rot roots, and AquaTome's own cycling guides plant first and then cycle. Keep the fish half: adding fish before the cycle is stable can kill them.

length.why: pH's facts hold the scale, the tank's range, raising and lowering it by each method with its caution and pace, and how it moves ammonia: more than 400 words carry. The chief of staff, 14 Nov 2026: 600, stop past 690.

write: Leave out lowering pH to about 6.0–6.5 during ammonia poisoning: no source gives a pace for that case, and it stood a few lines above "changing pH too fast can kill fish". Keep the 25–50% water change from the same line.
